summary_out.hypothesis: I expected the L1 monotone-yield arithmetic to continue DOWN the absolute-threshold axis: orders with |net_flow| in [0.5, 1.0) would be newly skipped on top of L4's set, and pnl would either continue rising (if the rule still holds) or stall/drop (if we had crossed the optimum). This was WRONG because the predicate's parameter has integer resolution on this oracle: net_flow only takes integer values (trade sizes are integer contracts), so |net|>=1.0 and |net|>=0.5 are EQUIVALENT predicates -- the interval (0,1) is empty. The pre-loop note implicitly flagged this ("trade sizes are typically integer contracts") but failed to recognize the consequence. CONTRADICTED. The brief-summary stream had everything it needed to predict this: L1 already established the threshold lever was acting on |net_flow|, and the L1-L4 trajectory mentioned integer trade counts; the lesson should have been internalized as 'threshold sweep must move by integer steps' before submitting L5.
summary_out.brief_summary: afg-b-l5 (aggressor-flow-gate brief-summary loop 5) attempted to FURTHER TIGHTEN the absolute threshold from L4's 1.0 -> 0.5 contracts (10s window, ratio leg absent). Result: PASS vs simple (+2415.61% pnl) AND beats base (+12.16% pnl) -- BUT bit-for-bit identical to L4 on every metric (pnl=$1088, sharpe=5.36, trades=86,089). Refinement targets vs L4: ALL FAIL (0.0 deltas). DIAGNOSIS: net_flow is the signed integer sum of trade sizes (integer contracts on this oracle), so the predicate set {|net|>=0.5} equals {|net|>=1.0} -- the interval (0,1) is empty. L5 is mechanically L4 in disguise. CRITICAL LESSON for future loops in the afg-b lineage: flow_threshold has INTEGER RESOLUTION on this oracle. Decimal-fraction tweaks below 1.0 (0.5, 0.25, 0.1, ...) are ALL no-ops and ALL equivalent to threshold=1.0. Any meaningful threshold change must move by at least one INTEGER step from the effective state. The threshold sweep's data is now: base(2)=$970/87,760, L4(1)=$1088/86,089 -- two points, gradient +$118 pnl / -1,671 trades from 2 to 1.
